 Posted November 20, 2026 at 10:35 am by Emma Cohn and David Cooper 
 Sixteen states will raise their minimum wages on January 1, lifting pay for over 6.6 million workers 
 Key takeaways 
 More than 6.6 million workers will get a raise starting January 1 as 16 states raise their minimum wages. 
 The increases will range from $0.26 an hour in Nebraska to $1.27 an hour in Michigan. 
 Michigan will be the latest state to reach at least a $15 minimum wage, joining 17 states and Washington, D.C. More workers will live in states with a $15 or greater minimum wage than in states with a $7.25 minimum wage. 
 Once again, localities in Washington state will have the highest minimum wages in the country. Tukwila, for example, will raise its minimum wage to $22.45, while the city of Burien could see a new rate of $22.49 if ongoing legal proceedings are resolved and the current law is upheld. 
 Raising the minimum wage is a simple, yet powerful way to make life more affordable for millions of working people. State and federal policymakers should ensure wage floors meet the needs of all workers. 
 Sixteen states will increase their minimum wages on January 1, boosting earnings for more than 6.6 million workers by a total of nearly $4.3 billion (see Figure A and Table 2 ). In addition, 48 cities and counties across the country will raise their minimum wages, lifting pay for even more workers.
 These increases are happening because state and local lawmakers, and in some cases voters, took action to help combat affordability challenges for low-wage workers across the country. With this month’s elections dramatically reshaping legislatures across the country, workers in many more states could see their paychecks grow if incoming lawmakers similarly act to raise their state wage floors.

 Our estimates account for both those directly and indirectly affected by the new minimum wage. To adjust their wage ladders to the new wage floor, employers often raise wages further up their pay scales, so some workers earning slightly above the minimum wage will also see a boost. We find that impacted workers will see an average increase in annual income of $645 (see Table 2). Affected workers in states with the largest minimum wage hikes, such as Michigan and Rhode Island, will see their pay go up by as much as $900 a year.

 Workers in two states won’t see promised raises 
 Although millions of workers will benefit from these changes in January, workers in two states with previously scheduled increases will not see their pay go up.
 In 2025, Missouri lawmakers passed a bill, HB 567 , which repealed the annual cost-of-living adjustments that voters had approved as part of a 2024 ballot measure, Proposition A. (The same bill also eliminated the statewide paid sick leave program that was part of Proposition A.) Workers will first feel the consequences of this law in 2027, when the legislature’s repeal of the inflation adjustment will cost an estimated 492,000 workers over $300 million in additional wages they otherwise would have earned. 1 
 Notably, the Missouri legislature will have a harder time undoing future voter-approved measures, as voters in the state passed a constitutional amendment this November prohibiting the legislature from repealing or amending future citizen-led ballot initiatives without 80% support in both legislative chambers and subsequent voter approval.
 In New York, the state’s minimum wage provision requires annual inflation adjustments unless a rise in unemployment or a drop in employment triggers an “ off-ramp .” Since the labor market has cooled in 2026, the “off-ramp” will take effect and freeze the minimum wage next year. While minimum wage increases may resume in 2028, this pause will deny much-needed raises to over a million workers in the short term and likely mean permanently lower wages for workers in the state overall in the long run. The rationale for the off-ramp provision was always dubious—poor economic conditions do not reduce the need for higher wages. If anything, they increase the need for strong income supports, whether through social insurance programs or wage increases. Governor Hochul has proposed a slight change to the law that could allow minimum wage rates to rise with inflation starting March 1, 2027, though it is pending approval by the state legislature.
 New state legislatures bring new chances to address affordability concerns and raise minimum wages 
 Although much of the affordability conversation centers around rising costs, state lawmakers have fewer tools at their disposal to control prices, many of which are set through global markets. However, affordability is not just about prices; it’s the outcome of a race between prices and incomes —and boosting incomes is where state policymakers have straightforward tools at the ready. Raising the minimum wage puts more money directly into the pockets of those who need it the most.
 In the recent 2026 elections, Democrats won new trifecta control of at least six states: Arizona, Michigan, Minnesota, Nevada, Pennsylvania, and Wisconsin. 2 Of these six states, neither Wisconsin nor Pennsylvania has a minimum wage law above the federal floor , and only Arizona has at least a $15 minimum wage. Lawmakers in these states, and the many others where pro-worker lawmakers have gained power, should prioritize passing substantial minimum wage increases that bring wage floors closer to true living wages .
 Legislators should also ensure that low-wage workers’ paychecks at least keep pace with inflation by indexing the minimum wage, which automatically adjusts it each year to reflect changes in prices. Twenty states and dozens of cities and counties across the country have enacted this straightforward policy. In fact, all but three of the state minimum wage increases taking effect this January are automatic inflation-linked increases.
 Lawmakers looking for even more powerful measures to boost incomes over the long run should target ambitious wage levels and then link the minimum wage to average or median wage growth. Because median wages typically outpace prices, wage indexing protects low-wage workers from rising costs and ensures their paychecks grow with improvements in the broader economy.
 Connecticut already links its automatic minimum wage adjustments to wage growth, while several other states and many localities maintain strong minimum wages that are indexed to inflation. Four states (California, Connecticut, Rhode Island, and Washington) and the District of Columbia will have minimum wages above $17 an hour this winter, and these minimum wages may reach $20 an hour by 2030.
 Table 3 shows that all but one of the localities raising their minimum wages in January have floors above $15 an hour. Additionally, seven localities in Washington and one in California already have or will have minimum wages above $20 an hour. And in Oakland, advocates have secured enough signatures to land a $30 by 2037 minimum wage initiative on a future ballot.

 Decades of economic research shows that raising minimum wages is an effective way to boost incomes for low-wage workers, with little if any impact on jobs. As lawmakers seek strategies for addressing households’ affordability concerns, this tried-and-true method should be high on their list.
 Notes
 1. Authors’ analysis using Economic Policy Institute Minimum Wage Simulation Model; 2021–2024 4-year ACS data pinned to 2025 CPS wage distribution. Employment scaled to match 2026 CPS labor force size. For more details see technical methodology .
 2. As of this writing, North Carolina’s state senate has one race outstanding, the outcome of which will determine control of the chamber. If the Democratic candidate wins, North Carolina will also be a Democratic trifecta.
